services.name: Marketing site
services.description: Nobody logs in. A few pages that load fast, read well on a phone, and come with working backups and sensible security headers.

services.name: API backend
services.description: The service layer on its own. Data model, documented endpoints, authentication and authorization, and a migration path that will not lock you in.

services.name: Web application
services.description: The API above, plus the interface people actually use. Accounts, screens, an admin side. One application rather than a whole product.

services.name: Product, first version
services.description: A web application plus the parts that make it a business: signup, billing, a marketing site, and the operations to keep it running.

services.name: Integration or migration
services.description: Moving off a dying system, or connecting two that were never meant to talk. With a rollback plan, not a hopeful weekend.

services.name: Engineering workflow audit
services.description: Days spent inside your process. Where the time actually goes, what breaks repeatedly, and a written plan ranked by hours saved per month.

services.name: Automate a manual process
services.description: The spreadsheet somebody rebuilds every Monday, or the data somebody copies between two systems by hand.

services.name: Deploy pipeline
services.description: Tests run automatically, deploys stop being an event, and rollback takes one command instead of an evening.

services.name: Monitoring and alerting
services.description: You find out about the outage before your customers tell you. Uptime, errors, certificates, and alerts worth waking up for.

services.name: Onboarding and documentation
services.description: Written so a new developer is useful in days rather than months, and so one person leaving is not an emergency.

services.name: Incident cleanup
services.description: Defaced, redirecting, flagged by Google, or suspended by your host. Entry point found, persistence removed, credentials rotated, delisting handled.

services.name: External exposure assessment
services.description: What an attacker sees before touching anything. DNS, TLS, headers, exposed panels, leaked credentials, known CVEs in what you run.

services.name: Secrets and access review
services.description: Where your keys live, who can reach them, how they rotate, and what already leaked into git history or a CI log.

services.name: Application security review
services.description: One codebase, read properly. Authentication, access control, injection, sessions, uploads, secrets, and the dependency chain.

services.name: Interface and usability review
services.description: Where your users get stuck, give up, or do the wrong thing. Every problem written down with the screen it happens on, ranked by how much it costs you, and a concrete fix for each one.
